jobs.title: Numerical Software Engineer Intern: Strategic Student Program at Siemens Digital Industries Software
jobs.description: Employer: Siemens Digital Industries Software - Digital Industries Software Expires: 11/13/2026 Numerical Software Engineer Intern: Strategic Student ProgramAbout Siemens Digital Industries SoftwareSiemens Digital Industries Software is a leading provider of solutions for the design, simulation, and manufacture of products across many different industries. Formula 1 cars, skyscrapers, ships, space exploration vehicles, and many of the objects we see in our daily lives are being conceived and manufactured using our Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software.Position OverviewWe are seeking a talented and enthusiastic Numerical Software Engineer Intern to join our geometric modelling team for a year-long industrial placement from July 2027 to August 2028. You will contribute to the development, testing and maintenance of a 3D boundary representation (B-rep) geometric solid modelling kernel used in advanced engineering and CAD applications. This is an excellent opportunity to apply mathematical and numerical knowledge to challenging real-world software problems while gaining experience in a professional development environment.What You Will Be DoingDesign, implement and maintain robust numerical algorithms for 3D solid modelling.Develop and enhance functionality within a boundary representation geometric modelling kernel.Investigate and resolve issues involving geometric accuracy, robustness, performance and edge cases.Write clear, efficient and maintainable production code, supported by appropriate unit and regression tests.Use debugging, profiling and code-review tools as part of a collaborative software development workflow.Work with experienced software engineers, mathematicians and application specialists to understand requirements and deliver reliable solutions.Contribute to work that uses AI to develop intelligent engineering tools and apply intelligent analysis to test logs, helping to identify patterns, diagnose issues and improve software quality.Document technical approaches, design decisions and test results clearly.What You Should BringEnrolled on a course that includes a year-long industrial placement.Sound knowledge of vector algebra and the ability to apply it to three-dimensional problems.Programming experience in C, C++ or another high-level programming language.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to numerical accuracy and detail.Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly and work effectively as part of a collaborative team.Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to learn unfamiliar mathematical and software concepts.Nice to HaveThree-dimensional geometry, geometric modelling or computational geometry.Numerical methods, numerical analysis or floating-point computation.Curves and surfaces, including non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS).Practical experience with artificial intelligence (AI), such as machine learning, generative AI, AI-assisted software development, or evaluating and integrating AI-generated solutions.Software development practices such as source control, automated testing and peer code review.What You Will GainHands-on experience developing production-quality numerical software for commercial CAD and engineering applications.Advanced knowledge of three-dimensional geometry, boundary representation modelling, numerical robustness and software performance.Practical exposure to modern development practices, including source control, automated testing, debugging, profiling and peer review.Experience using and critically evaluating AI assistance for real engineering challenges and code development.Mentoring and guidance from experienced software engineers, mathematicians and geometric modelling specialists.Stronger problem-solving, technical communication and teamwork skills within a professional engineering environment.Valuable career development through experience at Siemens, a global leader in engineering and technology innovation.Why UsAt Siemens Software, flexibility is how we work - hybrid by default, built on trust and autonomy. Together, 30,000 people across more than 200 countries build technology that shapes the real world. You'll grow through real projects, strong technical peers, and global mobility, backed by the scale and benefits of an industrial software leader. We're committed to equality and inclusion, and we hire based on merit, skills, and impact. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow!Our Commitment to Equity and InclusionWe value your unique identity and perspective. We are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society, while ensuring that we attract the best talent based on qualifications, skills, and experiences. We welcome you to bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us.Our Benefits & RewardsWe offer a comprehensive reward package which includes a competitive basic salary, bonus scheme, generous holiday allowance, pension, and private healthcare. We actively support working from home and flexible working arrangements. Siemens offers health and wellness benefits to employees; you can access the benefits available in your country via the link: https://jobs.sw.siemens.com/benefits/We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.Siemens Software. Transform the Everyday

jobs.title: Summer Games Software Developer Intern - San Diego, California at Booz Allen Hamilton Inc
jobs.description: Employer: Booz Allen Hamilton Inc Expires: 11/14/2026 University - 2027 Summer Games Software Developer Intern - San Diego, CAThe Opportunity: The Summer Games is an innovative internship program that attracts some of the nation’s best and brightest students. The goal is to develop a breakthrough idea or solution for one of our customer's most pressing, complex, and multidimensional problems while developing valuable technical skills. This competitive and collaborative program attracts thousands of applicants each year. Simulating a real-world startup accelerator environment, the interns are divided into teams, each working on a different challenge project. Throughout the Games, interns receive mentorship from senior leaders, solve problems using Booz Allen’s products and unique engagement models, and leverage the power of collaboration in a team environment. The summer culminates with a final Challenge Cup competition and presentation to senior leadership. A past winner took the challenge of helping blind individuals navigate by using new technology and developing a business and market penetration plan. Teams have also helped to develop an app that gives military commanders an easy way to track real-time and open-source information about developing situations, including sudden attacks, fighting human trafficking, and even tracking the spread of a disease worldwide. Join us. The world can't wait. You Have: Experience with programming languages, including Java, JavaScript, C, C++, Assembly, Python, Perl, R, or Bash Experience with machine learning, data mining, statistics, or graph algorithms in academic or internship environments Experience with conducting research and writing software Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Ability to work independently and in teams Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in a Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field by Summer 2028 or Summer 2029 Nice If You Have: Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Possession of excellent critical thinking and analytical skills Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. CompensationAt Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $52,900.00 to $108,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. Identity StatementAs part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. Candidate AI Usage PolicyAI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided. Work ModelOur people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration, whether it occurs in person or virtually. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen facility frequently, in alignment with leadership expectations and the needs of the role. You may also be required to work from or visit a customer facility.Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed at a Booz Allen office or customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role. jobs.title: Year Round Intern, Business Operations, Analysis, and Technology (R025902) at Federal Reserve Board
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Board Expires: 11/14/2026 SummaryThe Federal Reserve Board (Board) provides students opportunities for career success. The Board’s Internship program is designed to provide valuable work experience for undergraduate and graduate students considering careers including, but not limited to, economics, finance and accounting, information systems, and data analysis. The Board believes that by combining academic endeavors with project-related work experience, qualified and capable college students can gain the practical knowledge need in a competitive global job market. Internships are paid positions with salaries commensurate with credit hours; internships may be in-person, remote or hybrid, depending on the needs of the team. Employment in the Board’s internship program is granted to U.S. citizens. Applicants must be currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program at an accredited university and returning to continue studies after the internship. Interns receive a syllabus or research project plan outlining their projects and goals for the internship. Interns are assigned a supervisor or mentor to guide them through their internship, and regular check-in meetings with their manager to manage performance expectations and assist with learning goals. Interns have access to a wide range of training programs and events for professional development purposes. About the SectionThe Business Operations, Analysis, and Technology (BOAT) section provides strategic leadership for RBOPS through integrated technology operations, business operations, and financial management. We serve as expert consultants and strategic partners to division leadership and stakeholders. Position OverviewWe are seeking a highly motivated intern to support multiple functions within BOAT. This rotational position offers hands-on experience across information technology (IT), business operations, administration, data analysis, and business process improvement. The ideal candidate is analytical, detail-oriented, and eager to contribute to high-impact projects in a dynamic environment. Key ResponsibilitiesAs an intern, you will rotate through or support various functions, including: IT Operations & Network AdministrationImage and configure laptops for division staffManage hardware inventory and coordinate equipment deploymentsPick up and distribute Yubikey tokens and other security devicesProvide technical support and troubleshooting assistanceMaintain IT asset documentation and tracking systemsIT Program ManagementSupport project/program tracking and status reportingAssist with risk identification and mitigation planningHelp maintain project documentation and schedulesAdministrative SupportCoordinate meetings, including scheduling, calendar management, and room reservationsCoordinate logistics for team events, training sessions, and workshopsHandle ad hoc administrative requests to support section operationsData Analysis & Business IntelligenceConduct data analysis to identify trends and improvement opportunitiesDevelop visualizations and dashboards to support decision-makingSupport ad hoc analytical requests from division stakeholdersBusiness Process ImprovementDocument current-state processes and identify inefficienciesSupport change management initiativesAssist with knowledge management and documentation effortsEdit and review written materials for division leadership QualificationsRequired:Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Business Administration, or related fieldStrong analytical and problem-solving skillsProficiency in Microsoft Suite of tools (i.e., Word, PowerPoint, Excel); experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) preferredExcellent written and verbal communication skillsAbility to manage multiple priorities and work independentlyU.S. citizenship requiredPreferred:Experience with laptop imaging, hardware setup, or technical supportCoursework or familiarity with IT asset management and inventory systemsCoursework or experience in project management or business analysisCoursework or knowledge of process improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma)Experience with Artificial Intelligence (AI)Experience with SharePoint Online (SPO) is a plusExperience with programming languages (Python, R, SQL) is a plus What You'll GainExposure to Federal Reserve operations and payment systems oversightHands-on experience in IT operations, program management, administrative support, and data analyticsMentorship from experienced professionals in a collaborative environmentOpportunity to contribute to strategic initiatives that impact the divisionProfessional development in a prestigious government institution *This position requires onsite presence in the DC office*U.S. citizenship required

jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/14/2026 Reference Code USAMRDC-MRIID-2026-0008RHow to ApplyAll applications must be submitted through Zintellect at www.zintellect.comDescriptionThe Department of Defense (DoD) is offering a postdoctoral fellowship at the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command – Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRDC MRIID).What will I be doing? As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will engage in efforts to advance translational antiviral drug discovery. Research activities will include recombinant protein expression and purification, biochemical screening assay development, computational structural modeling, cell-based antiviral validation studies, and exposure to preclinical small-animal research models.Why Should I Apply? Under the guidance of a mentor, you will engage in research activities that include, but are not limited to: Designing, expressing, purifying, and characterizing recombinant viral and host proteins to support biochemical and structural studies. Applying computational tools to analyze protein structure and function, identify potential binding pockets, and map small-molecule interactions. Developing and using biochemical and cell-based assays to evaluate candidate antiviral compounds and investigate their mechanisms of action. Gaining experience with high-throughput phenotypic drug screening and anti-viral assays and applying promising therapeutic candidates in organoid and zebrafish disease models, with opportunities to support subsequent preclinical small-animal studies. Learning research that integrates protein science, computational analysis, and antiviral drug discovery with advanced disease models, including organoids and zebrafish, to evaluate promising therapeutic candidates. Where will I be located? Frederick, Maryland What is the anticipated start date? The USAMRIID is ready to make appointments immediately. Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and internships or fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified. What is the appointment length? Appointments are initially for one year with the option to extend the appointment for up to four additional years, contingent upon project needs and funding availability. What are the provisions? You will receive a stipend to be determined by MRIID. The stipend range for this opportunity is $70,000-$80,000/12-month appointment. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. Other provisions may include the following: • Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE) • Relocation Allowance • Training and Travel Allowance Security Clearance While participants will not enter an employment relationship with DoD or any other agency, this opportunity will require a suitability investigation/background investigation. Any offer made is considered tentative pending favorable outcome of the investigation.

jobs.title: 2027 Monarch Quantum Summer Internship Program at Monarch Quantum
jobs.description: Employer: Monarch Quantum Expires: 11/14/2026 The Monarch Quantum Summer Internship Program offers students the opportunity to work on cutting‑edge technology shaping the future of quantum computing. Interns join multidisciplinary teams and contribute to real engineering projects that support our quantum hardware, software, and system‑level development efforts.As a Monarch intern, you may help design or test components, build experimental setups, develop control or automation software, analyze system performance, or support integration of quantum‑safe technologies—depending on your background and interests. Interns collaborate closely with experienced engineers and researchers while gaining hands‑on experience in a fast‑moving, industry‑focused environment.We encourage applications from students who are curious, motivated, and excited to apply their technical skills to emerging quantum technologies. Opportunities are available for students at the bachelor's, master’s and PhD levels.Some project examples include:Develop a test fixture for assessing the stability of opto-mechanical bonds & assemblies and perform stability experiments. The intern will define test goals & requirements, execute mechanical & optical design of a fixture and test station, facilitate material procurement, build the assembly, execute testing, compile results, and deliver a presentation to engineering leadership. The intern will also participate in ongoing projects to gain exposure in a professional, high precision engineering environment.Work hands-on with an optically pumped semiconductor laser (OPSL) system in an ISO-7 (Class 10,000) cleanroom laboratory, collaborating with and mentored by junior and senior engineers as well as senior management. Intern project opportunities in this role include, but are not limited to, material characterization; device-level semiconductor laser characterization such as spectral analysis and power-efficiency measurements; and optical and thermal modeling using tools such as Zemax, COMSOL, SolidWorks, and ANSYS. Interns will gain practical experience across the full development cycle, from simulation and design through laboratory testing and analysis.Contribute to the optical design of components and lenses for next‑generation laser modules. Interns will help develop and design test stations used to evaluate both individual components and full module assemblies. The role includes hands‑on intern involvement in building and operating these test stations to collect and analyze performance data. The intern will also support the development and validation of new design methodologies for laser module engineeringSupport the development of advanced automated pick‑and‑place routines for a fully integrated robotic cell consisting of multiple 6‑DOF industrial robots. The project includes designing, implementing, and testing motion control algorithms that improve accuracy, speed, and reliability of component handling within the automated cell. The intern will collaborate with robotics engineers to develop end‑to‑end workflows, including path planning, error detection, sensor integration, and automation sequencing. In addition, the intern will help evaluate system performance, optimize cycle times, and contribute to documentation and validation of the robotic software stack.Design a reliability test station for cutting-edge photonics components. Develop requirements, procure parts, and build a test system that allows a laser to auto-focus into a micron-sized target. Interns will utilize CAD software to design the test layout and work directly to set up the experiment in a cleanroom laser laboratory environment. They will write a script in python or LabView to perform the auto-focusing calibration routine.Work alongside experienced engineers to design, analyze, document, and test electrical systems and prototypes. Intern responsibilities include schematic development, PCB documentation, data analysis, test execution, and supporting failure analysis and corrective actions. This project provides extensive opportunities for technical skill-building, mentorship, and exposure to professional electrical engineering practices.Support the build and test of existing and novel External Cavity Diode Laser (ECDL) products through hands on lab experiments. Interns will join the laser development team and will design and execute tests to prove components and full laser assemblies to support Monarch Quantum's mission to deliver high-quality light engines to our customers. Project opportunities include building and characterizing laser cavities with novel components, designing diode test stations, improving alignment processes, and modeling laser systems. Interns will be mentored by collaborating with senior scientists, management, and laser technicians. Interns will leave the experience with a strong theoretical knowledge of and hands-on experience with ECDLs.Focus on developing FPGA-based systems using hybrid C/C++ and HDL architectures, including designing interfaces to ADCs, DACs, microcontrollers, and other components. Interns will support the creation and testing of advanced data acquisition and analysis systems, participate in hardware‑firmware integration, and contribute to reviews, verification, and documentation.Support the development of automated optical assembly processes, with a focus on investigating adhesive properties and performance when bonding precision optics to metal components. Interns will design and execute experiments to characterize adhesive behavior, develop and refine process parameters, and evaluate the impact on optical performance and assembly quality. They will also receive hands-on training in optical alignment, precision motion systems, and robotic automation. This project will provide practical experience at the intersection of optics, materials, process development, and robotics.

jobs.description: Employer: Siemens - Smart Infrastructure Expires: 11/15/2026 Building Automation Design Engineer InternshipLocation: San Francisco area office, located in Fremont, CAUndergraduate: Rising Sophomore, Rising Junior, Rising SeniorDuration: 10 weeks Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7 or June 14, 2027 Hours: Full-time, 40 hours/weekHere at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you? Who designs your future? You do.Are you looking for an internship where you can showcase your technical aptitude and passion for problem solving to ensure customers can work in a comfortable, safe, and energy-efficient environment? Does gaining hands-on experience, real-world skills and valuable knowledge while developing yourself professionally sound exciting to you?Join our Siemens Smart Buildings Internship Program as a Building Automation Design Engineer Intern in Summer 2027! What is Building Automation?Siemens Building Automation Systems is a building management system (BMS) that automatically manages and controls all systems within a building. These systems include lighting, heating, cooling, ventilation, fire detection and notification, CCTV, door and window controls, water and waste management. It consists of sensors, controllers, software and communication devices. Siemens offers building automation systems for all building types and sizes, and for every use. The system is designed to manage a wide range of building systems, such as HVAC, lighting, security, fire safety, and other critical building functions. What you will do as a Building Automation Design Engineer InternThis internship is a 10 week program where you will rotate through various departments at the local Siemens office, all focusing on smart buildings and sustainable infrastructure. 80% of your time will be spent as a Design Engineer understanding the overall aspects of the role and related activities. 20% of your time with be spent with the Design Engineering Team Lead to understand the engineering role and engineering-related administrative tasksResponsibilities while working alongside our Engineering and Operations Teams include:Understanding project requirements and design build engineering solutions for higher education and K–12 education facilities, data centers, hospitals, pharmaceutical facilities, high-rise buildings, and lab facilities Preparing design documents, including system layouts, electrical drawings, bills of materials, sequences of operations, valve and damper schedules, and panel layouts as well as formatting and compiling submittals to Siemens L5 standard (unless established customer standard exists) Designing building network architecture to support operator workstations Analyzing plans, construction contract specifications, and codes to determine project requirements and risks Designing building and space pressurization solutions, chiller and boiler plant sequencing control, etc. Preparing engineering re-estimates and follow up with appropriate sales and management to ensure understanding of and satisfaction with job scope The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation.To apply for the Building Automation Design Engineer Internship Program, candidates must meet the following requirements:Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university Pursing an Engineering-related degree such as Electrical/Mechanical/Industrial Engineering, Construction Management, Computer – Aided Design and Drafting or related field of study Ability to work 40-hours per week for the 10-week program (May - July or June - August) Must be able to work on-site up to 3 days a week There is no relocation or housing stipend for this program Eligible candidate must be located within 50 miles of office location with access to a reliable vehicle, as this role does not provide transportation, housing or relocation support This program does not support students on a Visa such as F1, J1, M1 and H1B as well as OPT/CPTYou’ll win us over by having the following qualifications:Must be able to use hand tools, laptop, email, smartphone, and tablet Skilled in using Windows laptops and adept at learning new software related to building automation systems Ability to work in a team environment providing dedicated support to our customers Demonstrated leadership potential Strong analytical, We anticipate the job will require working up to 40 hours or more per week during the summer months with the potential for part time work or a co-op in the Fall of 2027. Interns will also have the opportunity to work with our Geotechnical Engineering team conducting subsurface investigations with exploration drilling crews. S. W. Cole Engineering is an established employee owned firm with a history of over 45 years of success and stable growth serving clients throughout New England. Job RequirementsCandidates must be able to follow verbal and written instructions to complete laboratory and field tests, have a general understanding of computers and ability to learn and use new software programs, and have the ability to read and learn to interpret construction specifications and plans. Familiarity with construction and/or engineering concepts is preferred, but not required. The physical and mental requirements for this position include lifting up to 75 pounds frequently, as well as moving heavier loads (such as 5-gallon buckets containing soil), stand for long periods of time, as well as move up and down from kneeling to crouching to bending. Must learn to properly operate company equipment, be able to properly transport samples and equipment over uneven ground with varying conditions (including tripping hazards, ice and snow, brush, construction staging, etc.). Requires close, distance, and peripheral vision. Ability to interact appropriately with a variety of individuals including but not limited to coworkers, supervisors, clients. Ability to remember and understand verbal and written instructions including laboratory test procedures. Ability to reason logically and make decisions. The Intern is occasionally exposed to variable and potentially extreme weather and temperature conditions. Applicants must have good verbal and written communication skills: Will be required to effectively communicate verbally to clients, project team members, supervisors and coworkers. Will be required to write effectively to take notes, record observations and data, and write emails and text messages on a daily basis. Candidates must be able to apply basic math skills for compiling and calculating data. Applicants must have reliable transportation, a valid driver’s license, active automobile insurance and an acceptable driving record. Education RequirementsCurrent college student with concentration studies in building construction, construction technology, construction management, geotechnical/civil/structural engineering, or related field.To apply for this position please complete the application including supplemental questions, submit a resume, and include a cover letter outlining how you meet the requirements for this position that are summarized above. jobs.description: Employer: Intel Corporation Expires: 11/19/2026 What if your next project helped power the future of technology? At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects. Collaborate with global partners and cross-functional teams. Build skills in communication, business strategy, project management, and data-informed decision making. Throughout your internship, you will collaborate with colleagues and global partners, contribute to impactful projects, and gain exposure to how Intel drives business impact across industries. This means you approach your work with a growth mindset and find ways to leverage AI to help make faster, smarter decisions that will 10X your impact at Box.Education & Placement Requirement: Currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree requiring a recognized 12-month industrial sandwich placement year before your final year of study (open to all academic disciplines; Business, Management, or Marketing is a plus, but not required).Growth Mindset & Curiosity: Demonstrates resilience, high energy, a proactive "can-do" attitude, and an eager appetite to learn about enterprise SaaS, cloud software, and AI technologies.Strong Communication & Interpersonal Presence: Articulate verbal and written communication skills with the confidence to build professional relationships with senior stakeholders across multiple channels.Commercial Acumen & Problem Solving: Analytical mindset with the ability to identify business trends, creatively uncover growth opportunities, and connect customer challenges to digital solutions.Organization & Detail Orientation: Strong time management skills, comfort prioritizing tasks in a fast-paced environment, and the ability to maintain high data quality and accuracy.Languages: Fluent German or French is an advantage but not requiredBox lives its values, with community and in-person collaboration being a core part of our culture.
